title: Top Secret
paragraphs: A 1950 espionage series starring Ilona Massey as Baroness Karen Gaza, placing its heroine in stories of international intrigue and intelligence work connected with Europe and World War II.
NBC sustaining espionage drama starring Ilona Massey as Baroness Karen Geza/Gayzer. Historical run contains 19 numbered assignments.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Monday opening period (June 12, 1950 to July 10, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Sunday period (July 23, 1950 to August 20, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Friday period (September 1, 1950 to September 8, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Monday return (September 18, 1950 to September 25, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Ilona Massey (performer), Fred Collins (announcer), Harry W. Junkin (writer, director, and producer), Roy Shield (composer and conductor), Allan Stevenson (performer), Brook Byron (performer), and Luis Van Rooten (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to international espionage, World War II intelligence operations, counterintelligence and undercover identity, sabotage and counter-sabotage, and rehearsal and transcription preservation.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes World War II espionage setting, Transcribed/rehearsal preservation, and NBC summer Top Secret run.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-chase|The Chase]], [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], and [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]].
